newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end firm off highs on bonds, lira.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end firm off highs on bonds, lira.

text.p: Italian shares closed firmer but off session highs on Tuesday, underpinned by strength in Italian bonds and futures and the lira.
Traders said Wall Street also gave a hand in good afternoon business after a hesitant start due to the delay in trading of stock futures and options because of technical problems.
The all-share Mibtel index ended 0.93 percent up at 10,545 after high at 10,563 and the Mib30 blue chip index closed 0.98 percent higher at 15,791 after high at 15,820.
"There was a lot of technical trading closely tied to movements of the FIB bourse futures index," one trader said after derivatives finally trading got underway just after midday.
Insurances were mostly well bid, with Alleanza up 3.55 percent to 11,755 lire and La Fondiaria gaining 1.55 percent to 5,825. But Fiat's Toro insurance unit lost 1.64 percent to 20,493.
Fiat ended up a modest 0.07 percent at 4,359. Energy group ENI was up 0.25 percent at 7,966 lire but was off its day's opening high of 8,000.
Pirelli performed well, ending up 1.57 percent at 2,854 lire, on positive sentiment over the group's delopment plan, traders said.

Olivetti was largely ignored, closing 0.34 percent off at 528.5 lire despite expectations of imminent sell-offs and TV and advertising group Mediaset's declared interest in the Olivetti-controlled Omnitel GSM mobile phone operator.
Mediaset ended up 1.15 percent at 7,291 lire.
Carlo De Benedetti's financial holding Cofide ended at 740 lire after being suspended limit down and a low at 717.
Food group Parmalat which has a big market in South America, ended up 2.81 percent up at 2,452, gaining from the lira's current exchange rate.
